findings.source: AxelarGateway.sol:538 if (isCommandExecuted(commandId)) continue; :564 _setCommandExecuted(commandId, true); :569 if (success) emit Executed(commandId); else _setCommandExecuted(commandId, false); with key keccak256(abi.encodePacked(PREFIX_COMMAND_EXECUTED, commandId))
findings.issue: The same storage key is printed three ways: as a hash of raw memory in the duplicate check and in the reset after a failed command (the 'un-execute' write), and as sha3(PREFIX, _279) in the set; the reader cannot see that the failed-call path clears the flag it just set.
findings.rule: Resolve a hashed buffer built at b = mem[64]: words stored at b + 32 and b + 64 and the length 64 at b give sha3(mem[b + 32 len 64]) = sha3(w1, w2) (free-pointer folding as in the known P2 root cause); a one-element concat(mem[0]) key holding such a hash is that hash.

notes: Source loops (2, both whiles): execute's command loop (1325: duplicate check, 6-way command-hash dispatch, allowOperatorshipTransfer as the loop-carried s, self-call with the chosen selector, Executed event or reset) and setTokenMintLimits' loop (424, 'while True' with the exit test first). Implicit whiles (25): ABI decoding of the transaction (bytes32[], string[], bytes[], 1238-1307), copies of strings and call buffers, including copies of constant length printed as loops ('while idx < 68' at 636/1789, 'while idx < 100' at 683/723: the abi.encodeWithSelector buffers of 4 + 2 or 3 words; see c00007's finding on constant-trip copies). The self-call's arguments stay raw memory (the selector is variable, mem[... len 4] = _348 >> 224). The tails 1362-1431 repeat the key buffer writes and the set store in each dispatch arm (P12). The command functions (mintToken, burnToken, deployToken, approveContractCall*, validateContractCallAndMint, callContractWithToken) were reviewed by reading; faithful.
summary: Faithful text with both source loops found; the main command loop is readable, but the command-executed key is hidden behind raw-memory hashes on two of its three uses, and call buffers are copied by loops, some of constant length.
